name: Gaofen-1
reported_objects: 3 objects, 13x18 m, 14x19 m, 24x22 m, within 20 km radius
region: Gulf of Thailand / South China Sea
source: SASTIND website via Xinhua; ABC News 13 Mar 2014 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-03-13/aircraft-fail-to-find-floating-objects-in-hunt-for-mh370/5317810 ; Malay Mail 13 Mar 2014 https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2014/03/13/chinese-satellite-seeking-mh370-finds-objects-at-sea/634023
notes: Aircraft searched the position on 13 Mar and found nothing. Chinese officials later said the images were released by mistake and did not show debris (ABC caption). Image footprint not published.

name: Gaofen-1
dates_utc: 2014-03-18 (time not published; 'around noon' Beijing ~04:00 UTC); released 22 Mar
reported_objects: 1 object, 22.5 x 13 m
source: SASTIND as quoted by PTI/Deccan Herald and ABC News 22 Mar 2014 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-03-22/missing-malaysia-airlines-plane-mh370-debris-china-satellites/5339092 ; project note research-satellite-imagery-2014.md (b)
notes: Position 44 deg 57 min S 90 deg 13 min E (some outlets misprint as 44.57/90.13 decimal). AMSA plotted it inside the 22 Mar search area; not sighted. Footprint not published.

name: Chinese constellation (unnamed; 10 then 20-21 satellites)
dates_utc: from 2014-03-10/11; '20 satellites' stated 18 Mar; '21' by 22 Mar
reported_objects: none published beyond the two Gaofen-1 detections
region: all regions (SCS, Malacca, northern corridor over China, SIO)
source: Malay Mail 11 Mar 2014 (PLA Daily) https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2014/03/11/china-deploys-satellites-in-search-for-missing-mh370/632903 ; Malay Mail 18 Mar 2014 (Foreign Ministry) https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2014/03/18/china-says-has-20-satellites-looking-for-missing-malaysian-jet/637353 ; Charter activation page ('China utilised ten of its satellites')
notes: Satellite names other than Gaofen-1 were never published; the count includes navigation, weather and communications satellites. Ziyuan-3, HJ-1, Yaogan use is plausible but NOT FOUND in any source.

name: International Charter 'Space and Major Disasters' (activation)
operator: Charter members; requestor and project manager China Meteorological Administration
reported_objects: none published
region: South China Sea (location of event as recorded)
source: Charter activation page (Internet Archive capture read 20 Oct 2026) https://disasterscharter.org/web/guest/activations/-/article/missing-malaysia-airlines-jet
notes: The activation page names no contributing satellites and shows no products. Member agencies (CNES, ESA, CSA, DLR, ISRO, JAXA, USGS/NOAA, CNSA, KARI, INPE, DMCii, Roscosmos, EUMETSAT, UAE/EIAST) could have contributed; none is documented. No image footprints published.

name: Terra / Aqua (MODIS, ASTER) and ISS sensors (ISERV)
reported_objects: none published (detection limit stated as ~30 m)
region: Gulf of Thailand / SCS, then southern Indian Ocean
source: NASA statement reported by IBTimes 13 Mar 2014 https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/malaysia-airlines-flight-mh370-nasa-searching-satellite-data-crash-sites-1440112 and Universe Today 23 Mar 2014 https://www.universetoday.com/articles/nasa-targeting-earth-observing-satellites-and-iss-sensors-to-aid-missing-malaysian-airline-search
notes: Data sent to USGS EROS Hazards Data Distribution System. MODIS belongs to the cloud layer; ASTER (15 m) is in the spec table. No scene list published.

name: Terra MODIS (NASA Langley, Minnis et al.)
dates_utc: polar-orbiter imagery 2014-03-07 19:00 to 2014-03-08 05:00 UTC; candidate at 04:45 UTC 8 Mar
reported_objects: one linear feature, judged 'probably a shadow from some other feature or a cloud edge'
source: ATSB 2017 Operational Search for MH370, PDF pp.126-127 (read in project note)
notes: Search for an impact signature on 8 Mar, not for floating debris. A Sumatra candidate judged a cloud-deck discontinuity.

name: WorldView-2
dates_utc: image 2014-03-16 04:16 UTC; passed to AMSA 20 Mar; released 20 Mar
reported_objects: Object 1 approx 24 m at 43 58 34 S 090 57 37 E; Object 2 approx 5 m at 44 03 02 S 091 13 27 E (-44.0506, 91.2242)
source: DIGO sheets DIGO-00718-01/02-14 (read in project note); DigitalGlobe statement quoted by ABC News 21 Mar 2014 https://abcnews.com/US/colorados-digitalglobe-found-objects-malaysia-airlines-search/story?id=22988405 ('captured on March 16 by our WorldView-2 satellite at a resolution of approximately 50 cm')
notes: AGO reviewed DigitalGlobe imagery frame by frame. Aircraft searched 20-23 Mar without relocating the objects. Image footprint and catalogue ID not published. DigitalGlobe said it continued to task its satellites over a wide area around the detection.

name: DigitalGlobe constellation (WorldView-1, WorldView-2, GeoEye-1, QuickBird, IKONOS) via Tomnod
dates_utc: Tomnod campaign from 2014-03-10/11; 24,000 km2 by 13 Mar, +14,000 km2/day; SIO imagery added progressively from ~20 Mar
reported_objects: no confirmed detections published; 645,000 user tags by 13 Mar, 4.7 million tags overall
region: Gulf of Thailand / SCS, Strait of Malacca / Andaman, then southern Indian Ocean
source: Malay Mail 13 Mar 2014 https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2014/03/13/satellite-crowdsourcing-adds-2-million-searchers-for-mh370/634203 ; Quartz 12 Mar 2014 https://qz.com/188270 ; NBC 20 Mar 2014 https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/missing-jet/satellite-data-dump-slows-hunt-traces-missing-plane-n58306 ; Bremner 2015 (project note B1)
notes: Tomnod tile footprints were visible on the site in 2014 but no footprint dataset has been published. Which spacecraft produced which tiles is not public.

name: Foreign-government imaging request (France, Italy, Germany, Thailand, China, United States)
reported_objects: seven detections 16-27 Mar in 43-45 S, 90-97 E, objects 5-24 m (ATSB)
source: ATSB 2017 Operational Search for MH370, PDF pp.125-126 (read in project note)
notes: ATSB names the countries but not the satellites. Confirmed spacecraft from other sources: Pleiades 1A (France), THEOS (Thailand), Gaofen-1 (China), WorldView-2 (US commercial). Italy, Germany and US government systems: NOT published.

name: Request to US, China, France 'amongst others'
reported_objects: none
source: Malaysia MOT press statement 16 Mar 2014 (read in project note S4)
notes: Separate from the AMSA/AGO request.

name: Pleiades 1A
operator: French Ministry of Defence / CNES; re-analysed by Geoscience Australia 2017
dates_utc: 2014-03-23 ~04:00 UTC (CSIRO '~4Z'); first French analysis Mar 2014; GA analysis Mar 2017
reported_objects: 4 scenes ~25 x 20 km, ~100 km apart, centred near 35 S 91 E (34.4-35.4 S); 70 objects, 12 'probably man-made', 28 'possible'; French MoD first found 4 objects
source: GA Record 2017/13 https://www.atsb.gov.au/sites/default/files/media/5773373/mh370_satellite-imagery-geoscienceaust-report.pdf ; ATSB 2017 PDF p.127; CSIRO Part III EP174155; ATSB news 2017 https://www.atsb.gov.au/news/2022/mh370-satellite-imagery-analysis
notes: Per-object positions in GA Tables 1-4. Scene corners not published (GA holds metadata). Area never searched by air in 2014. CSIRO back-tracked to a most likely impact at 35.6 S 92.8 E.

name: Airbus Defence and Space imagery ('122 objects')
dates_utc: image 2014-03-23 (time not published); received by MRSA 25 Mar; released 26 Mar
reported_objects: 122 potential objects in ~400 km2, 1-23 m; 11 tabulated 2.99-23.79 m near 44.66-44.70 S, 90.43-90.62 E
source: Malaysia MOT press statement 26 Mar 2014 and 'Maps showing objects reported by MRSA' (read in project note S5/S6); NBC 26 Mar 2014 https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/missing-jet/mh370-satellite-images-show-122-potential-objects-n62356
notes: Spacecraft not named (Pleiades 1A/1B or SPOT 6 are the Airbus candidates). Fox News (AP) reported Airbus mobilising five satellites. Full 122-object list and footprint not published. Positions were inside the 26 Mar aerial search area; nothing found.

name: 'French satellites' radar images
reported_objects: 'potential objects in the vicinity' (MOT); ATSB: radar and optical detections 20-23 Mar in 34-35.5 S, 90-92 E
source: Malaysia MOT statements 23-24 Mar 2014 (read in project note S4); Malay Mail 23 Mar 2014 https://www.malaymail.com/amp/news/malaysia/2014/03/23/malaysia-jet-search-focuses-on-satellite-images-floating-debris/640415 ; ATSB 2017 PDF p.126
notes: France has no civil radar satellite; independent analysis attributes the 21 Mar radar detections to Italy's COSMO-SkyMed (next row). Never searched by air; two merchant ships reported nothing.

name: COSMO-SkyMed (satellite not identified)
operator: ASI / Italian MoD (Italy); disclosed by an unnamed source to V. Iannello
dates_utc: 2014-03-21 (pass time not published; project treats dawn-20Mar/dusk-21Mar as alternatives)
reported_objects: 3 objects: 34.9519 S 91.6833 E; 34.5742 S 91.8689 E; 34.7469 S 92.1725 E (centroid given in lat/lon columns). Project also holds a 4th contact F4 at 35.3853 S 89.9539 E (source: project memory, Pete)
source: Iannello 2021 https://mh370.radiantphysics.com/2021/07/23/italian-satellite-may-have-detected-mh370-floating-debris/ ; Airline Ratings 2021 https://www.airlineratings.com/articles/three-new-pieces-suspected-mh370-debris-revealed ; project memory mem_367e91bf34de (F1-F4)
notes: Never officially released. 'Wide-angle, low-resolution capture' (ScanSAR class), with a later high-resolution pass attempted. Mode, incidence, look side and footprint not published. Italy is one of the countries ATSB lists as asked for imagery.

name: THEOS (Thaichote)
dates_utc: 2014-03-24 03:07:56 UTC (incidence 26.98 deg); delivered to Malaysia 27-28 Mar
reported_objects: ~300 objects, 2-16 m, over >450 km2; zones near 46 28-46 31 S, 89 21-89 38 E (provisional, read from thumbnails)
source: GISTDA image sheets and news 27 Mar 2014 (Internet Archive; read in project note S11/S12); NBC 27 Mar 2014 https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/missing-jet/mh370-thai-satellite-spots-300-objects-near-suspected-crash-site-n63461
notes: Zone 4 sheet not archived. Object list and footprint not published. Search moved 1,100 km NE on 28 Mar before follow-up.

name: IGS (Information Gathering Satellite; spacecraft not disclosed)
reported_objects: ~10 objects within 10 km radius of 44 17 S 90 56 E; largest ~8 x 4 m
source: AFP via Malay Mail 28 Mar 2014 https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2014/03/28/japan-satellite-images-show-floating-objects-possibly-from-mh370-reports/642893 ; Kyodo/Jiji via VIR https://vir.com.vn/japan-satellite-images-show-floating-objects-possibly-from-mh370-26696.html
notes: Images withheld as 'highly confidential'; only the position passed to Malaysia. Candidate spacecraft: IGS Optical 3/4/5-demo or Radar 3/4 (spec table). 00:00-06:00 UTC = 09:00-15:00 JST window given to the press, not the pass time.
